messages.subject: Re: Help! Maven configuration with Netbeans and Renjin
parts:
It looks like the issue is unpacking the jar. One of the serialized functions "$<-person" is maybe not a valid file name on windows.

This might be something we could change in the future, but in the meantime, is it really neccessary to unpack the jar as part of your build?

Alex

Hi Antoine,
I don't have any experience with JavaFX or really with JNLP so I'm not quite sure how to guide you. 

I wonder if it's possible to embed the jars upon which you depend into the final artifact rather than mushing all the classfiles together in a single jar? IIRC, this is what the one-jar tool does, though again I don't know if something similar is possible with JNLP.

The quickest fix would be to run your build on Un*x or OSX system, perhaps with VirtualBox or on Travis CI?

I can understand this isn't ideal, so if you may want to open an issue on GitHub regarding the way symbols are named.

Best,
Alex

Le mercredi 21 février 2018 11:40:30 UTC+1, Alexander Bertram a écrit :
Hi Antoine,
I don't have any experience with JavaFX or really with JNLP so I'm not quite sure how to guide you. 

I wonder if it's possible to embed the jars upon which you depend into the final artifact rather than mushing all the classfiles together in a single jar? IIRC, this is what the one-jar tool does, though again I don't know if something similar is possible with JNLP.

The quickest fix would be to run your build on Un*x or OSX system, perhaps with VirtualBox or on Travis CI?

I can understand this isn't ideal, so if you may want to open an issue on GitHub regarding the way symbols are named.

Best,
Alex
